episode_title: Maria Braune - Be a Therapist for Your Customers

real_qa.q: Why does customer advocacy matter for B2B companies like DailyPay in today's market?
real_qa.r: Customer advocacy matters because it creates genuine brand identity by letting customers drive the marketing message rather than relying solely on company-created materials. Voice of the customer builds trust and credibility with prospects, and it helps with retention and sales. When prospects see that everything about DailyPay comes from their actual users and customers, it demonstrates authentic listening to feedback and creates a network of proven advocates that new customers can reference.

real_qa.q: How should customer success managers approach asking customers to participate in advocacy activities without damaging relationships?
real_qa.r: Position the ask by considering what else the customer has on their plate, not just their satisfaction with your product. Understand their organizational context, seasonal demands, and timing constraints before making requests. For example, with DailyPay's HR and payroll customers, avoid making asks during open enrollment or seasonal peak times. Show you've done your research on their situation, and customers will appreciate that you're thinking about their needs before they have to tell you it's a bad time.
real_qa.requete: how to ask customers advocacy participation

real_qa.q: What approach helps customers agree to produce customer stories and advocacy content?
real_qa.r: Position it by asking customers to remember their own buying journey: 'What are some of the things that you wish you knew or had heard or content that you had when looking at us?' This brings them back to the buyer's mindset and helps them see they can help their community by sharing what they learned. Then ask if they'd be willing to help produce that material. Customers respond positively when they understand they're helping others in their tribe and industry, not just doing the vendor a favor.
real_qa.requete: how to get customers agree to advocacy stories

real_qa.q: How can customer advocates participating in speaking opportunities and visibility build personal professional brand?
real_qa.r: Advocates who participate in speaking events, webinars, and industry platforms gain personal recognition and professional credibility. One DailyPay customer mentored a team member and had him take on a speaking role at an interactive email marketing event, which both excited the mentee and demonstrated the mentor's leadership. This type of visibility makes advocates feel important, opens their eyes to new opportunities with your company, and can create ripple effects where they introduce other talented people from their organization to serve as advocates.

real_qa.q: How does DailyPay use customer feedback to refine product positioning and understand their target market?
real_qa.r: DailyPay conducted a 'man on the street' campaign in New York asking people about on-demand pay. They discovered that different age groups and industries had different perspectives on the product, and some said they would never use it. Rather than forcing those prospects into an advocacy role, Maria uses that feedback to refine positioning—for example, highlighting the savings feature rather than emergency access. This helps the company understand who their true persona is and allows customers offering the benefit to their employees to know who to pitch it to.
real_qa.requete: using customer feedback refine product positioning

real_qa.q: What technique maximizes output from a single customer conversation for multiple marketing use cases?
real_qa.r: In a 45-minute to one-hour conversation, Maria prepares mini versions of different initiatives in advance. She gathers their bio and background, captures quotes for later use, asks buyer journey questions to understand their decision process, collects data for case studies, and identifies speaking opportunities. This positions the conversation efficiently so she can extract buyer journey information, quick quotes, case study material, and product insights all at once, rather than needing multiple separate calls with the same customer.

guest.bio_context: Maria has built her career around relationship building, starting as a client success manager and running onboarding teams before moving into advocacy and customer marketing. She joined DailyPay at the end of November after previous experience in product marketing and advocacy roles. Her background spans from early telecom days through email marketing before transitioning to customer advocacy and marketing.
